questions: What is the actual exit-code contract of nightly-health.yml and its boundary step?
Are the boundary findings advisory or enforcing by design?
What is the composition of the current 18 github_surface findings?
Which writer produced the absolute-path audit.json target, and can it still emit one?
Do prior unsealed sibling plans already hold a mechanism for any of this?

findings.claim: The boundary step is documented reports-only in three places and returns 1 on findings into a bare run: with no suppression, so it fails the job.
The two genuinely enforcing steps both refuse to fail via set +e and captured exit code, so the lifecycle can read them; the advisory step is the only hard-failing step.
Measured harm: status_json exits 1 today on governance-index/stale-tier1 with overall_ok false, and no health issue is open. Five consecutive job failures 2026-09-05 to 2026-09-09.
evidence: gh run list --workflow=Nightly Health -> 5 consecutive failures

findings.claim: main() is three-valued (2 could-not-scan / 1 findings / 0 clean); continue-on-error would suppress 2 as well and must not be used.
The 18 findings are 5 detector-specification examples, 12 genuine outside-repository references, and 1 drive-letter path in an issue body. None is a code defect.
The boundary-lint marker was applied to the tracked copy of a specification table and dropped on the pull-request body copy; scan_text applies it per line on both surfaces.
GH #465 writer-side premise fails measurement: the artifacts are remediate-iter1.json, hold no top-level target, and contain no absolute path; git grep over tracked files returns nothing.
evidence: git grep over tracked files: 0 hits

findings.claim: Phase 268 documented this defect accurately and scoped it out; no plan in the corpus holds a mechanism.
No test pins that a step documented reports-only cannot fail the job.
